claims.text: What the strip looks like QRS positive (dominant R) in II, III and aVF and negative (dominant S) in lead I.
claims.quote: QRS is POSITIVE (dominant R wave) in Lead II, Lead III and aVF QRS is NEGATIVE (dominant S wave) in Lead I
claims.locator: How to recognise right axis deviation

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Axis: greater than +90° (90° to 180°)
claims.quote: An axis of 90° to 180° is considered right axis deviation

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Mechanism: anything that raises pulmonary pressure and causes right ventricular hypertrophy — cor pulmonale, acute PE, pulmonary hypertension; sometimes RBBB or left posterior fascicular block
claims.quote: it occurs in any condition that increases pulmonary pressures and causes right ventricular hypertrophy (cor pulmonale, acute pulmonary embolism, pulmonary hypertension), and it sometimes occurs in right bundle branch block or left posterior fascicular block.

claims.text: Left posterior fascicular block, lateral MI, RVH, acute lung disease (e.g., PE), chronic lung disease (e.g., COPD), ventricular ectopy, hyperkalemia, sodium-channel blocker toxicity, WPW
claims.quote: Left posterior fascicular block Lateral myocardial infarction Right ventricular hypertrophy Acute lung disease (e.g. Pulmonary Embolus) Chronic lung disease (e.g. COPD) Ventricular ectopy Hyperkalaemia Sodium-channel blocker toxicity WPW syndrome

claims.text: Normal in children and in thin adults with a vertical heart
claims.quote: Normal in children or thin adults with a vertically positioned heart

notes.issue: "Treatment is directed at the cause" quoted Merck Treatment of Arrhythmias, which does not cover axis deviation.
notes.resolution: Claim and its Symptoms and treatment label removed from the block.
